name: Reconnaissance
description: Information gathering and footprinting techniques used to profile targets before active exploitation.
tips: Always start with passive recon. Document everything. Use multiple sources to cross-reference findings.
examHabits: Screenshot every discovery. amass enum --passive saves JSON; import into Burp. Check crt.sh for alternate domains.

name: Network Enumeration
description: Host discovery, port scanning, and service enumeration across segmented networks. Layer 2/3 discovery, SNMP, NetBIOS, and SMB enumeration.
tips: ICMP is often filtered. Use TCP SYN ping, ARP ping, and masscan. Segment awareness is critical — missing an IP = missing a zone.

name: Active Directory
description: Windows Active Directory enumeration, exploitation, and post-exploitation techniques for enterprise environments.
tips: Enumerate first, exploit later. BloodHound is your best friend. Check for constrained/unconstrained delegation.
examHabits: Always enumerate SRV records first (nslookup _ldap._tcp.domain). Try null session before credential attacks. BloodHound is your map — study the shortest path.

name: Web Applications
description: Web application penetration testing including OWASP Top 10, API security, and modern web frameworks.
tips: Check every input field. Burp Suite is essential. Don't forget business logic flaws.
examHabits: Use Burp Proxy constantly. ffuf with SecLists. Try SQLi before XSS — SQLi gives broader access. Check /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml.

name: Binary Exploitation
description: Buffer overflows, format strings, heap exploitation, and shellcode development for Linux and Windows binaries.
tips: Always check protections first (canary, NX, PIE, RELRO). GDB with pwndbg is essential. Ghidra for reverse engineering.
examHabits: Run checksec + file first. Use ROPgadget for gadgets, one_gadget for quick wins. libc-database: search by puts/fgets GOT address.

name: IoT / Firmware
description: IoT device firmware analysis, embedded systems exploitation, hardware debugging, and radio communications.
tips: Extract firmware first. Look for hardcoded credentials. Check UART/JTAG interfaces. Bus pirate is your friend.
examHabits: binwalk -e firmware first. Check for default creds in /etc/passwd, web configs. UART is the most reliable hardware path — try 115200 baud.

name: Privilege Escalation
description: Techniques for escalating privileges from low-level shells to root or SYSTEM on Linux and Windows systems.
tips: Run linpeas/winpeas first. Check SUID binaries, sudo misconfigs, cron jobs, and kernel exploits. Document every step.
examHabits: Linux: sudo -l, find SUID, writable dirs. Windows: whoami /priv, check service perms, AlwaysInstallElevated. Google Cloud Shell for offline hash cracking.

name: Lateral Movement
description: Moving between compromised hosts across network segments using pivoting, SSH tunnels, pass-the-hash, and relay techniques.
tips: Chisel and ligolo-ng are essential for pivoting. Know when to use each. SOCKS proxy with proxychains for TCP tools.
examHabits: Document every pivot. SSHuttle > proxychains. Check port 445, 135, 139, 445 open first. Use ligolo for clean tunneling.

name: Password Attacks
description: Hash cracking, online brute forcing, password spraying, and credential reuse strategies using hashcat, John, and Hydra.
tips: Identify hash type first. Try dictionary + rules before brute force. Reuse every credential found immediately across all hosts.
examHabits: Use rockyou.txt first. Hashcat rule: best64.rule. For Kerberoasting, crack offline. For AS-REP, online. Always check for NULL bind.

name: Post Exploitation
description: Post-exploitation activities including credential dumping, persistence, C2 communication, and data exfiltration.
tips: Harvest credentials early. Establish C2 before moving laterally. Clean up artifacts before the exam window closes.
examHabits: Screenshot flags immediately. Dump hashes with lsadump::lsa /patching. Use Mimikatz in memory. Beacon stays alive for 6+ hours — don't kill it.

name: Exploitation Frameworks
description: Automated exploitation using Metasploit, Searchsploit, and specialized frameworks for IoT and router exploitation.
tips: Searchsploit first for quick wins. Metasploit for reliable, repeatable exploits. Routersploit for IoT-specific targets.
examHabits: MSF: db_nmap, use exploit/multi/handler. Searchsploit for CVE modules. Load .rc files for repeatable workflows.

name: Reporting
description: Note-taking, evidence collection, screenshot documentation, and final report generation for penetration test deliverables.
tips: Document as you go, not at the end. Use tmux for organized sessions. Screenshot everything with flameshot.
examHabits: Flag format is usually CPENT{...}. Screenshot each flag. Use OBS or flameshot. Name files clearly.

name: CTF Challenges
description: Capture the Flag methodologies covering cryptography, steganography, forensics, and miscellaneous challenges.
tips: Read the challenge carefully. Check file headers with binwalk. Stegsolve for image steganography. CyberChef for encoding.
examHabits: steghide steghide steghide. Check metadata with exiftool. Try CyberChef for decodes. XOR with common keys.

name: Defense Evasion
description: Techniques for evading antivirus, EDR, firewalls, and other security controls during penetration testing.
tips: Obfuscate payloads, use living-off-the-land binaries, and understand how AV/EDR products detect malicious activity.
